text:
2.2 Parallel Bootstrap (One bootstrap per iteration):
Set up the cluster and Run a parallel version.


Code
cl <- makeCluster(detectCores() - 1)
registerDoParallel(cl)

set.seed(1)

time_parallel_single <- system.time({
  boot_parallel_single <- foreach(i = 1:B, .combine = c) %dopar% {
    median(sample(x, replace = TRUE))
  }
})

time_parallel_single


   user  system elapsed 
   2.45    1.03    3.53 


Note: We observe that parallel is much slower than serial. This could be due to the fact that each bootstrap task is tiny. You’re asking workers too: - receive a task - run one median computation - send result back The communication and coordination overhead dominates the actual computation time, and so this version shows that naive parallelisation can be slower than serial.

Note



This website contains my completed Statistical Computing assignment, including implementation, results, and performance comparisons between replicate, foreach, and parLapply. All results are reproducible (where applicable) and code is provided in full.

title: Statistical Computing Assignment
text:
1 Overview
This assignment focuses on two core ideas:

Bootstrap / simulation workflows in R for estimating quantities of interest.
Parallel computing tools and best practices, including:

foreach (sequential and parallel)
parLapply (cluster-based parallelism)
runtime comparisons and overhead considerations
reproducibility challenges (random number generation in parallel)
